newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama sees global role with telecom privatization.
newsitem.headline: Panama sees global role with telecom privatization.

text.p: Panama will become "a channel for global telecommunications" with the partial privatization of state telephone utility INTEL scheduled for later Tuesday, a top government official said.
"These two companies understand Panama's strategic value. Panama will be transformed into a type of channel for global telecommunications," INTEL director Juan Ramon Porras told local RPC radio.

Telecommunications giants GTE Corp of the United States and Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc are the only companies that have qualified to participate in the sale of 49 percent of the National Telecommunications Institute (INTEL).
Porras said the partial phone sale would allow Panama to participate in fiber optic projects because either winner has a strong international presence and access to capital.
"INTEL has been signing submarine fiber optic agreements which would connect us to the American continent," he said. He did not provide more details.
Although INTEL is said to be worth $2 billion, government officials have not given estimates of its value.
The government estimates the winner of Tuesday's auction will invest at least $500 million over five years in upgrades, and increase the number of telephone lines to 800,000 from 330,000.
